{"world_model":"W4 after E008. Measured: E005 (SGD+EMA, 9ep) 0.7583 at 9.10s. E006 (Muon, bs2000) 0.7649 at 9.45s. E007 (Muon+EMA+resize 24/28/32) 0.7590 at 7.33s. E008 (same at 8.5ep) 0.7572 at 6.98s.

Beliefs:
1. Time is compute-bound and scales with pixel count times epochs. Resizing saved about 2.1s, and my prior was too pessimistic about it. Halving an epoch saved about 0.35s, so one epoch costs about 0.7s. Fixed cost is about 0.5-1s (prepare, whitening, data upload, first-step effects). That fixed cost caps what epoch cuts and CUDA graphs can gain.
2. Accuracy gains from EMA (+1pp), Muon (+0.6pp) and the other changes were real. Resizing cost about 0.6pp, and E008's half-epoch cut cost only 0.18pp. That is the low end of my predicted slope, so the margin is slightly better than I feared. I scored a hit on E008.
3. Noise. Compiled runs are near-deterministic per seed, but any recipe change reshuffles the trajectory. The 3-seed-mean accuracy noise from such changes is about 0.15-0.25pp, so anything under 0.3pp is unresolvable. Time noise is about 1-2% (0.1s). The 40-seed mean is probably 0.1-0.3pp below the 3-seed mean. At 0.757 against the 0.75 judgment bar we have about 0.5pp of true margin, which is thin but probably fine.
4. Regression: E005-E007 gains partly came from lucky trajectories. Small tweaks (LR floor to 0, BN recompute, width 512) are most likely null. They give at most +-0.2pp, and I would not bank them.
5. Further time cuts must come from fewer pixels, less width or fewer epochs, and each costs accuracy. Costs are roughly 0.2pp per 0.5 epoch, about 0.5pp for the more aggressive resize schedule, and about 0.2pp for width 512. The bar is 0.753, so there is room for roughly one more of these, not all of them.
6. The code shown has epochs 9.5 in HYP, which conflicts with E008's stated 8.5. I am treating the measured tip as the baseline.

W4 after E008. Measured: E005 (SGD+EMA, 9ep) 0.7583 at 9.10s. E006 (Muon, bs2000) 0.7649 at 9.45s. E007 (Muon+EMA+resize 24/28/32) 0.7590 at 7.33s. E008 (same at 8.5ep) 0.7572 at 6.98s.

1. Time is compute-bound and scales with pixel count times epochs. Resizing saved about 2.1s, and my prior was too pessimistic about it. Halving an epoch saved about 0.35s, so one epoch costs about 0.7s. Fixed cost is about 0.5-1s (prepare, whitening, data upload, first-step effects). That fixed cost caps what epoch cuts and CUDA graphs can gain.
2. Accuracy gains from EMA (+1pp), Muon (+0.6pp) and the other changes were real. Resizing cost about 0.6pp, and E008's half-epoch cut cost only 0.18pp. That is the low end of my predicted slope, so the margin is slightly better than I feared. I scored a hit on E008.
3. Noise. Compiled runs are near-deterministic per seed, but any recipe change reshuffles the trajectory. The 3-seed-mean accuracy noise from such changes is about 0.15-0.25pp, so anything under 0.3pp is unresolvable. Time noise is about 1-2% (0.1s). The 40-seed mean is probably 0.1-0.3pp below the 3-seed mean. At 0.757 against the 0.75 judgment bar we have about 0.5pp of true margin, which is thin but probably fine.
4. Regression: E005-E007 gains partly came from lucky trajectories. Small tweaks (LR floor to 0, BN recompute, width 512) are most likely null. They give at most +-0.2pp, and I would not bank them.
5. Further time cuts must come from fewer pixels, less width or fewer epochs, and each costs accuracy. Costs are roughly 0.2pp per 0.5 epoch, about 0.5pp for the more aggressive resize schedule, and about 0.2pp for width 512. The bar is 0.753, so there is room for roughly one more of these, not all of them.
6. The code shown has epochs 9.5 in HYP, which conflicts with E008's stated 8.5. I am treating the measured tip as the baseline.

Unsure: the true 40-seed mean. Whether CUDA graphs help (Muon's compiled update and the many small launches may be CPU-bound under the 4-CPU pin). Whether the 20px phase hurts more than linearly. Whether LR to 0 helps once EMA is on.

forecasts.reason: With EMA the LR floor matters little; any gain is under 0.3pp and within trajectory noise. Time is unchanged.
Compute falls about 15% on the variable part, saving roughly 0.8s, but the 20px phase likely costs about 0.5pp. That leaves it near the 0.753 bar.
The last group is a small share of FLOPs at low resolution, so the saving is about 3-4%. The accuracy loss is within noise.
The held-out seed mean should land within 0.3pp of the seeds 0-2 mean, probably slightly below it. The per-seed std is about 0.2pp.
Fixed overhead and compute dominate, so the gain is about 3% at most. There is a real risk of capture issues with compiled Muon and the changing resolutions.
The Lookahead already averages the BN buffers, so recomputing them gains little, probably under 0.3pp. It adds about 0.05s.

cruxes: What is the true 40-seed mean accuracy of the current recipe (I013)? If it is below 0.752, no further time cuts are feasible.
How much of the ~7s is fixed cost (prepare, data upload, first-step warm-up) versus per-epoch compute? A large fixed share caps what I011, I012 and I014 can save.
Does the 20px phase hurt accuracy superlinearly? This decides whether I011 stays above 0.753.
